name: JavaScript
description:
Adversaries may abuse various implementations of JavaScript for execution. JavaScript is a platform-independent scripting language (compiled just-in-time at runtime) commonly associated with scripts in webpages, though JavaScript can be executed in runtime environments outside the browser.(Citation: NodeJS)

JScript is the Microsoft implementation of the same scripting standard. JScript is interpreted via the Windows Script engine and thus integrated with many components of Windows such as the [Component Object Model](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1559/001) and Internet Explorer HTML Application (HTA) pages.(Citation: JScrip May 2018)(Citation: Microsoft JScript 2007)(Citation: Microsoft Windows Scripts)

Adversaries may abuse various implementations of JavaScript to execute various behaviors. Common uses include hosting malicious scripts on websites as part of a [Drive-by Compromise](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T0817) or downloading and executing these script files as secondary payloads. Since these payloads are text-based, it is also very common for adversaries to obfuscate their content as part of [Obfuscated Files or Information](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027).

Within industrial control system networks, adversaries most commonly abuse the use of JavaScript on overlap assets that run on operating system platforms similar to Enterprise devices.

telemetry.name: Module Load
telemetry.description: A module or library being loaded into a running process.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope Sysmon ImageLoad (7) to lab processes/paths; retain module hash, signer and destination process. Inventory alone does not prove a module loaded.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

strategies.name: Behavioral Detection of JavaScript Execution in ICS

analytics.name: Analytic 2092
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies wscript.exe/cscript.exe/mshta.exe or other JScript execution from unexpected parents/paths, especially when followed by child interpreters, network connections, or system modification. Alert only when the interpreter is not part of the asset's approved software/automation baseline or its execution context violates an approved signer/hash/path/parent/user rule, and require OT-relevant corroboration such as access to engineering files, ICS software/API use, communications with protected OT assets, configuration change, or another suspicious follow-on behavior. Suppress documented vendor software, engineering workflows, diagnostics, backup, patching, and approved maintenance.

tuning.description: Allowed script hosts and vendor applications

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Sysmon
log_sources.channel: EventCode=7; scripting-engine module loads when useful

analytics.name: Analytic 2093
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies node/nodejs or another JavaScript runtime launched from an unexpected service, web process, scheduled task, user, or path, followed by outbound connections, shell execution, persistence, or OT-relevant access. Alert only when the interpreter/shell is not expected for the asset role or user/service context, or when its parent, path, arguments, remote-session source, or follow-on behavior violates the approved OT baseline. Suppress approved engineering scripts, vendor support, diagnostics, backup, patching, and maintenance windows.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: execve for node/nodejs or JavaScript runtime and child processes

log_sources.name: linux:osquery
log_sources.channel: socket_events for runtime-originated connections, where deployed

software.name: REvil
software.description: [REvil](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0496) utilizes JavaScript, WScript, and PowerShell scripts to execute. The malicious JavaScript attachment has an obfuscated PowerShell script that executes the malware. (Citation: Tom Fakterman August 2019)

references.description: Tom Fakterman 2019, August 05 Sodinokibi: The Crown Prince of Ransomware Retrieved. 2021/04/12

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.description: Restrict untrusted web content and active scripting on ICS workstations, jump hosts, and other overlap assets, especially where browser access is not required for operations.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.description: Use application control to restrict wscript.exe, cscript.exe, mshta.exe, Node.js, and other JavaScript runtimes to approved paths, parent processes, scripts, and users.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.description: Disable or remove JavaScript/JScript execution surfaces that are not required for the documented role of an ICS asset, while preserving validated HMI, vendor, and engineering dependencies.

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.description: Harden browsers, HTML applications, and Windows scripting hosts that can execute JavaScript/JScript on ICS overlap assets.

simulation.prerequisites: Use a process simulator or isolated test rig with no connection to production controllers or physical actuators. Preserve safety interlocks; destructive effects require synthetic evidence, not real equipment damage.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
